The idea

How it works

Every person who enters the system gets one opportunity in the Patient Journey pipeline. Workflows move that opportunity from stage to stage when something happens: a form is submitted, a booking is confirmed, or staff mark a visit as showed, cancelled or no show. Tags remember who the person is, so the next workflow knows what to do.

Click any stage to see how it connects

Scroll sideways on small screens

The key idea

The opportunity is the patient journey

Each workflow starts by looking for the person's existing opportunity. If it finds one, it updates it. If it does not, it creates one. The pipeline stays free of duplicates, even when someone requests the guide, books, cancels and rebooks.

Why it mattersOne person, one record. The booking workflow, the follow up workflow and the cancellation workflow all find the same opportunity, so the stage always shows the true status. Nobody has to merge or tidy anything.
Step 1 · The pipeline

One pipeline, five stages

A pipeline called Patient Journey shows where every person is. The stages are simple on purpose, and each one is moved by an automation.

StageWhat it meansHow a person gets there
New LeadShowed interest, has not bookedRequests the free guide. Workflow 1 creates or updates the record.
Appointment BookedA visit is scheduledBooking confirmed. Workflow 2 moves or creates the record.
Appointment CompletedThe patient attendedStaff set the status to Showed. Workflow 3 moves the record.
Cancelled / No ShowCancelled or missed the visitStaff set the status. Workflow 4 moves the record.
Lead Nurture CompletedFollow up finished, no bookingThe last follow up email is sent. Workflows 1 and 4 move the record.
Step 2 · The funnels

Two funnels, two kinds of visitor

Some visitors want information first. Others are ready to book. Each gets a path built for them.

Free guide funnel

For visitors who are not ready to book yet.

  • Opt in page. Free Dental Checkup Guide, with a short form: full name, email and a consent checkbox.
  • Thank you page. Confirms the guide is on its way.
  • Behind the scenes. The form starts Workflow 1.

Appointment funnel

For visitors who are ready to book.

  • Landing page. Trust points, "What brings you in?", services, how it works, FAQ.
  • Booking page. Choose a service, pick a time.
  • Thank you page. Confirms the appointment, explains what happens next and shows the clinic's contact details. A confirmed booking starts Workflow 2.

The lead magnet

A five page guide the lead can keep

The free guide is a branded PDF: how to prepare for a visit, the services, what to expect, when to seek prompt care and questions to ask the dental team. It ends with a Book Now button, so the guide leads straight to the booking page.

Crownwell Dental Checkup Guide

The PDF the lead receives right after submitting the form. Click the page to enlarge it, or use the thumbnails to flip through.

  • Cover. What is inside, and a clear next step.
  • Before your visit. What to bring, what to ask, what happens.
  • Services. The five services and typical appointment lengths.
  • After your visit. Healthy habits and when to seek prompt care.
  • Your next step. Four booking steps and a Book Now button.

Step 4 · The memory

Twelve tags keep the workflows in sync

Tags are how one workflow tells the next one what happened. Workflows read them to decide what to send, and write them to record what they did.

GroupTagsUsed for
Lead source
lead-guide
Marks people who asked for the free guide
Patient type
new-patientreturning-patientvip-patient
Recognising first time, returning and VIP patients
Appointment status
bookedrescheduledcancelledno-show
Showing the current state, and stopping follow up when someone books
Emergency
emergency-cancelledno-show-cancelled
Separate handling for urgent visits
Outcome
wonnurture-completed
Recording a completed visit, or a finished follow up
Patient type logicBooking promotes, cancelling steps back. A first booking sets new-patient. Booking again sets returning-patient, then vip-patient. If a visit is cancelled or missed, the patient type steps back one level, so a visit that never happened does not count.
Step 5 · The human step

The one step done by hand

Whether a patient showed up is a human fact, so the system asks for it at the right moment. That one answer starts either the follow up workflow or the cancellation workflow.

1
The appointment time arrivesWorkflow 2 sends the team an internal reminder to update the appointment status.
2
Staff set the statusShowed, Cancelled or No show, in the appointment.
3
The status triggers the next workflowShowed starts Workflow 3. Cancelled or No show starts Workflow 4. Emergency visits have their own triggers.
Step 6 · The communication

Branded where it counts, personal everywhere else

Not every email needs a template. Four moments get a branded design to catch the lead's attention: the guide, the appointment confirmation, the thank you after a visit and the review request. Everything else is a clean, personal note, so it reads like a message from the clinic, not a newsletter.

Click an email to enlarge it. Screenshots use a test contact.

The personal follow up emails

Thirteen emails are written as clean, personal notes from the clinic, with no template or heavy design, so they read like a message from a person. Pick a group, then an email, to read each one as the lead sees it. Highlighted brackets are details GoHighLevel fills in for each contact.

EmailWorkflowStyle
Guide delivery1Branded
Follow up series (3 emails)1Personal
Appointment details2Branded
Reschedule notice and reminders (1 day and 2 hours before)2Personal
Thank you after the visit3Branded
Check in and review request3Branded
Cancellation and no show emails (standard and emergency)4Personal
Missed visit follow up series (3 emails)4Personal
The thinkingDesign where attention matters, keep it personal where trust matters. A branded email stands out at the moments a lead is paying attention. A personal, text-first email feels like it was written for them, which suits reminders and gentle follow up.

Step 8 · Beyond the happy path

Edge cases the system handles

A system is only as good as its worst day. These are the situations it was designed for.

SituationWhat happens
Lead requests the guide but does not bookTimed emails run, then the person moves to Lead Nurture Completed so the team can see the sequence has finished.
Lead books during the follow upA goal step sees the booked tag and stops the emails.
Person already existsEach workflow looks for an existing opportunity first, so no duplicates are created.
Appointment is rescheduledIts own path: tagged, new details emailed, team alerted, not treated as a new booking.
Cancelled or no showTagged, emailed, moved to Cancelled / No Show, then followed up.
Emergency visit cancelled or missedSeparate triggers, tags and emails for the Emergency Dental Visit service.
Patient rebooks after a missed visitWorkflow 2 clears the old tags, so they start a clean journey and any running follow up stops.
Staff forget the status updateA reminder alert goes to the team at the appointment time.
The impact

What this does for the clinic

The goal was to take repetitive follow up off the front desk and make sure no lead, booking or missed visit goes quiet. Here is how the system helps day to day.

01Fewer leads slip awayEveryone who requests the guide gets it straight away, then about 23 days of timed follow up that stops the moment they book. The team is alerted to each new lead.
02Every visit is confirmed and remindedA branded confirmation and two personal reminders go out automatically, and rescheduled visits are handled on their own path.
03Less manual adminOne record per person, no duplicates, and tags and pipeline stages update on their own. Staff only set the visit status.
04The team stays informedAlerts for new leads, bookings and reschedules, plus a reminder at appointment time if the status has not been updated.
05Missed visits are followed upCancelled and no show patients get a personal email, then about 18 days of follow up, with separate handling for emergency visits. Rebooking ends it.
06Patients feel looked afterA thank you an hour after the visit and a check in with a review request the next day, in branded and personal emails.
A note on resultsThis is a demonstration build, so no performance figures are claimed here. Numbers such as booking rate or no show rate can only be measured once the system runs with real clinic traffic.
